facts.label: Tagline
facts.value: Ship better code. Catch bugs earlier.
facts.sentence: VERCODE is the AI code review a team actually reads: deterministic static analysis runs first, task-routed AI reasoning runs on the bounded diff, and the result is published back to the pull request as a verdict plus evidence-backed inline findings.

facts.label: Open source?
facts.sentence: The VERCODE source is open under the MIT license. The hosted service runs on a publicly installable GitHub App.

facts.label: Self-hosted?
facts.value: pipeline runs on your provider keys; the service is hosted
facts.sentence: VERCODE analyzes code; it does not execute the pull request's own tests in the current release. The review pipeline runs in VERCODE's service; enterprise organizations can route model calls to their own providers via BYOK or a self-hosted Ollama deployment.

facts.label: Review latency p50
facts.sentence: A review is published to the pull request in under 120 seconds at p50, from webhook receipt to GitHub publication.

facts.label: Review latency p95
facts.sentence: 95% of reviews are published within 300 seconds of webhook receipt.

facts.label: Default reviews per month
facts.sentence: A standard organization quota includes 50 reviews per month; the cap is configurable per account.

facts.label: Files per review
facts.sentence: A review processes up to 100 changed files on a heavy-usage quota; larger diffs degrade to the highest-risk files with a note.

facts.label: Default confidence floor
facts.sentence: Findings below the confidence floor (default 0.6) are not posted by default; the floor is configurable per organization.

facts.label: Where source code is stored
facts.sentence: VERCODE reads the pull request diff and bounded context; it does not store your source repository in its database. Findings are retained for the retention window, then purged.

facts.label: GitHub App permissions
facts.sentence: The VERCODE GitHub App requests the least-privilege scope set: contents:read, pull_requests:write, checks:write, metadata:read, issues:read. It does not request admin:org or any secrets scope.
